title: Apply project rules only to registered workspaces
when: Before a tool guard evaluates a workspace
need: Machine guards apply outside projects; managed project rules use the registered checkout mapping. Broken scope or authority cannot hold Stop, SessionStart or SessionEnd. Repair the named infrastructure failure before resuming work; tool and prompt refusals remain enforced. Native Stop reentry always allows, and repeated identical holds exhaust their allowance after three blocks within five minutes. Machine privacy, literal search quoting and unmatched path-glob guards apply outside projects. Main-commit, destructive-Git and lane authority rules apply in managed projects. Registered Git worktrees share the main checkout mapping; nested independent repositories do not. The client proves Git metadata using Git common and per-worktree directories and reports it through the existing ignored write-target fact for local and HTTPS evaluation. Only the source-write guard excludes proven metadata; missing proof stays protected, and destructive Git and ownership checks remain authoritative. Refusals suggest actual held-lane source destinations, including new files, but never children of a worktree .git file; refresh installed client hooks to restore missing metadata proof.
surface: Shared client-local and server hook dispatch
gap: Candidate scope is covered by regression tests; deployed installed-harness delivery is unproved. See guard-scope-live-delivery.
review: Source and candidate tests; no live delivery claim.
